data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":["SRC_002"],"disanalogies":["Population statistics require multiple runs; the problem asks for within-run evidence.","Statistical comparison requires a baseline; within-run evidence must be self-contained."],"overturn_conditions":["A single engine is shown to have a perfect false-claim rejection rate, making statistical comparison moot.","The problem is reframed as demanding a logical, not empirical, standard of independence."],"shared_structure":["Both single-engine and cross-engine verification can be evaluated by false-claim rejection rates.","Both involve a trade-off between independence and convenience."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002"],"transfer_claims":["The standard for scientific replication (statistical indistinguishability) transfers to engine verification.","The burden of proof transfers to the single-engine advocate to show comparable performance."]},"claim":"The necessity of engine separation is a contingent, empirical question, not an a priori necessity.
